svg.title: HVCL01 two-node Hyper-V host and storage topology
svg.desc: Conceptual Windows Server 2025 single-site cluster HVCL01 has HV01 and HV02 with identical pNIC aliases. HostVM combines Management and Compute through a SET virtual switch on pNIC01 and pNIC02, connected to separate switch paths A and B. Each host management vNIC uses example VLAN 10. App01 runs only on HV01 with a guest vNIC on example VLAN 120; the HV02 guest attachment is a migration-target placeholder, not a second running VM. The Storage intent uses dedicated physical pNIC03 on path A and VLAN 711, and pNIC04 on path B and VLAN 712, without a storage virtual switch. Existing SMB endpoints are reachable on both storage networks. Repeated A and B labels identify the same physical switches. ATC does not configure those switches, file-service endpoints, or guest IPs.
svg.metadata: Conceptual educational diagram for Windows Server 2025 only. Embedded icon geometry is reused from: C:\Azure-Icons\CnE_Enterprise\Server (generic).svg; C:\Azure-Icons\compute\10021-icon-service-Virtual-Machine.svg; C:\Azure-Icons\networking\10080-icon-service-Network-Interfaces.svg. Original viewBoxes and aspect ratios are preserved. Not runtime output.
svg.text: HVCL01: two hosts, two intents, redundant paths
Single-site Hyper-V example · identical pNIC aliases on HV01 and HV02 · VLANs are design inputs.
SET uplinks use pNIC01 on path A and pNIC02 on path B.
No storage vSwitch in this design. Both storage networks reach the existing SMB file service.
A/B labels repeat the same redundant physical switches; SMB boxes are views of the same existing service.
ATC does not configure physical switches, file-service endpoints, or guest IPs.
App01 is active only on HV01. The HV02 guest attachment represents its migration target.
